sections.title: All the place and time words
sections.content: You know a family of words that follow a bare noun. Place: *alatt, fölött, előtt, mögött, mellett, között, körül*. Time: *előtt, után, közben*. And the new ones: *körül* (around), *közben* (during), *nélkül* (without), *felé* (towards), *helyett* (instead of). One sentence can use several: *Ebéd előtt a park felé sétálunk.* (Before lunch we walk towards the park.)

sections.title: Same rule every time
sections.content: The noun stays bare and the postposition comes after it. The thing you choose instead gets its usual ending: *Kávé helyett teát kérek.*

items.spanish: Ebéd előtt a park felé sétálunk.
items.english: Before lunch we walk towards the park.
We meet in front of the gate.

items.spanish: Ebéd után a pad mellett pihenünk.
items.english: After lunch we rest next to the bench.

items.spanish: Kávé helyett teát kérek, cukor nélkül.
items.english: Instead of coffee I would like tea, without sugar.

sections.content: If a place word seems to need an ending, check: the noun before a postposition has none. *A pad alatt*, not *A padban alatt*.
